classification.difficultyReason: Decompose each figure into two regions, find the missing triangle height in part a, and combine the component areas.

content.prompt: Find the area of the composite shapes.

spec.description: An upper triangle joined to a lower trapezium, retaining the change in outer-edge slope at their horizontal shared boundary. Four double-ended dimension arrows label the shared width, lower height, bottom width and total height.
spec.mathematics: Shared base 10 cm; bottom base 14 cm; trapezium height 6 cm; total height 19 cm. The triangle height is obtained by subtraction.
spec.answerVisibility: All dimensions and the internal boundary remain visible in the unsolved question. No areas or derived lengths are printed.

answer.short: $137\text{ cm}^2$; triangle $65\text{ cm}^2$ plus trapezium $72\text{ cm}^2$.
answer.worked:
Let $A_1$ be the triangle's area and $A_2$ the trapezium's area.
$$\begin{align*}h_1&=19-6\\h_1&=13\text{ cm}\\A_1&=\frac{10\times13}{2}\\A_1&=65\text{ cm}^2\\A_2&=\frac{6(10+14)}{2}\\A_2&=72\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{Total}}&=65+72\\A_{\text{Total}}&=137\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: An upper trapezium joined to a lower parallelogram whose top is shifted right. Retains the horizontal shared boundary and all five dimension annotations.
spec.mathematics: Trapezium parallel sides 6 cm and 12 cm with perpendicular height 5 cm. Parallelogram base 12 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied dimensions and the shared boundary remain visible in the unsolved question. No calculated areas are printed.

answer.short: $105\text{ cm}^2$; trapezium $45\text{ cm}^2$ plus parallelogram $60\text{ cm}^2$.
answer.worked:
Let $A_1$ be the trapezium's area and $A_2$ the parallelogram's area.
$$\begin{align*}A_1&=\frac{5(6+12)}{2}\\A_1&=45\text{ cm}^2\\A_2&=12\times5\\A_2&=60\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{Total}}&=45+60\\A_{\text{Total}}&=105\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
